items.title: Mississauga council sworn in — new mayor’s 1st directive is tax freeze
items.summary: Mayor Alvin Tedjo pledges affordability, economic growth and innovation at city hall as Mississauga kicks off its 2026-2030 term. Mississauga’s city council, newly elected for the 2026-30 term, at the inaugural ceremony on Nov. 16. Mississauga’s newly elected city council was sworn into office on Nov. 16 at the Living Arts Centre, marking the start of the 2026-30 term. Along with Mayor Alvin Tedjo, nine incumbent councillors and two newcomers took their declarations of office before a nearly full main auditorium. Tedjo received prolonged applause and a standing ovation from the audience and council colleagues after receiving the mayor’s chain of office — the ceremonial regalia presented to a mayor upon taking office — and during his inaugural address. Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services’ pipe and drum band performed at the inaugural ceremony on Nov. 16. The ceremony opened with a band procession by Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services’ pipe and drum band, a national anthem performance by Catherine and Chloe Tiongson and an Indigenous drum circle performed by Little Creek Singers . An Indigenous drumming circle at the inaugural ceremony by Little Creek Singers to give Indigenous blessings.

items.title: Motorcyclist suffers life-threatening injuries in crash with minivan in Mississauga
items.summary: A motorcyclist suffered life-threatening injuries and another person was taken to hospital after a collision involving a motorcycle and a minivan in Mississauga. Peel Regional Police say the crash happened Tuesday afternoon (Nov. 17) on Dundas Street West near Fifth Line. m. after the motorcycle and minivan collided. An adult male riding the motorcycle was taken to hospital in serious condition. A second person was also transported to hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries, according to additional reporting by CityNews. The circumstances surrounding the collision have not been released, and police have not indicated what may have caused the crash. Westbound Dundas Street was closed between Fifth Line and the collision scene while officers investigated. Drivers were advised to use alternate routes. The closure caused traffic disruptions in the area during the afternoon commute. Peel Regional Police have not released the identities or ages of those involved.

items.title: Tedjo offers few details on where Mississauga will find savings to deliver two-year tax freeze
items.summary: Alvin Tedjo began his tenure as Mississauga’s new mayor Monday evening with one big question on the minds of taxpayers: how will he deliver the two-year tax freeze he promised in return for votes. Following the city’s inauguration of its new council on November 16, Tedjo reiterated his commitment to affordability and the need for City Hall to become more financially efficient during a media scrum with reporters. However, when asked repeatedly how he intended to achieve those savings, the new mayor offered few specifics about which departments, expenditures or internal operations he would examine to make the numbers work. He repeatedly said efficiencies need to be found, leaving taxpayers waiting for a clearer picture of what his promised tax freeze will mean for the city's finances. “Right now, the burden is on residents. I think before we ask residents to tighten their belts even further, we need to tighten ours, so the city has a responsibility to make sure that we're not the cause of people's financial problems, and that's what I'm doing and I think our first budget is going to show that we can get this done,” Tedjo said. When speaking with reporters following the inauguration of Mississauga’s new city council, Mayor Alvin Tedjo provided few answers on where his administration will finding savings and efficiencies to make good on his campaign promise of a two-year tax freeze. (Benjamin Steeves/The Pointer) Tedjo’s tax commitment became the central part of his mayoral campaign, as he positioned himself as the candidate who could deliver the biggest savings for voters. Unprotected Floor Opening at Mississauga Wastewater Plant Led to $100,000 OHSA Fine
items.summary: According to the Ontario Ministry of Labour, the Ontario Clean Water Agency was fined $100,000 after pleading guilty to an Occupational Health and Safety Act offence tied to a workplace fall in Mississauga. The ministry says a worker was critically injured after falling through an unprotected floor opening at a wastewater treatment facility on Nov. 30, 2023. Workers were installing a new motor pump that day, and the job required opening floor hatches at several levels so a crane could lower the motor to a lower subfloor, the ministry said. An electrician and a helper opened the hatches and prepared the area, and a maintenance lead was then told about an issue and told workers to go to lunch, according to the ministry. The agency, which provides water treatment services across Ontario, pleaded guilty in Provincial Offences Court in Mississauga on Sept. 28, the ministry reported.

items.title: Westbound Dundas Street Closed After Motorcycle and Minivan Collide Near Erin Mills Parkway
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Paramedic Services, two people were taken to hospital after a motorcycle and a minivan collided in Mississauga near Dundas Street West and Dunwin Drive, just west of Erin Mills Parkway, on Tuesday. Paramedics said the motorcyclist was transported to a trauma centre in serious, life-threatening condition, while the minivan's occupant went to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Peel Regional Police told CTV News Toronto the minivan's driver stayed at the scene. Const. Tyler Bell-Morena said the motorcyclist, an adult male, is in serious condition at a trauma hospital but was alert when he left the scene. Police closed westbound Dundas Street West from Fifth Line for the investigation and are asking drivers to use alternate routes.

items.title: Metrolinx Offers Presto Prizes for Rider Feedback on Mississauga's 18-Kilometre Transitway
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Metrolinx is surveying riders at the Mississauga Transitway's 12 stations as part of a push to improve the $528 million bus rapid transit corridor. The provincial transit agency says the 18 kilometre route, built with MiWay and running from Winston Churchill Boulevard to Renforth Drive, fully opened to passengers in 2017. Transit officials are asking riders to complete an online survey by Dec. 4, with five participants eligible to win a $75 Presto card load, the outlet reports. Three years after the transitway opened, ridership fell by nearly 91 per cent when the COVID-19 pandemic struck in 2020, according to insauga.com. The outlet says feedback from the survey will help shape future improvements across the network as officials work to rebuild ridership on the route.

items.title: New restaurant in Mississauga will be among six opening in Canada
items.summary: Last Updated November 17, 2026 at 1:30 pm A new restaurant that’s coming to Mississauga’s Heartland Town Centre is among six that are scheduled to open in Canada before the end of the year. The fast-casual restaurant chain Chipotle Mexican Grill announced on Tuesday that it is continuing its Canadian expansion with new locations set to open in Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta. Chipotle serves burritos, burrito bowls, tacos, quesadillas, salads and more. “The momentum we’ve built in Canada throughout 2026 is carrying through to year-end and reflects the opportunity we continue to see for Chipotle in the market,” said Anat Davidzon, the managing director of international at Chipotle. ” READ MORE: Restaurant chain opens first Milton location Chipotle said it’s on track to grow its footprint in Canada by approximately 30 per cent in 2026.

items.title: Zero Percent Tax Increases Ordered for 2027 and 2028 Budgets in Tedjo's First Act as Mayor
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga Mayor Alvin Tedjo used his first address to the new city council on Monday night to order city staff to deliver zero property tax increases in both the 2027 and 2028 budgets. Tedjo made the announcement at the Living Arts Centre, where he and 11 councillors took their oaths of office at the inaugural meeting of the 2026 to 2030 council, the outlet reports. He said he had spent two years telling voters taxes needed to be frozen and called this his first official act as mayor, according to insauga.com. Tedjo defeated former mayors Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie in the Oct. 26 election after making affordability the central theme of his campaign, the outlet said. He told council that life has become more expensive than ever and that residents need a break, insauga.com reported.

items.title: Winston Churchill Boulevard Arrest Ends Hour-Long Chase After St. Catharines Cellphone Store Robbery
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Ontario Provincial Police arrested five suspects on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Mississauga a little over an hour after a robbery at a business on Vansickle Road in St. Catharines on Sunday afternoon. The outlet reports five men pulled up to the shop in a stolen vehicle, forced their way inside, and stole an unspecified number of cellphones before fleeing. Niagara Regional Police's Criminal Investigations Bureau took over the case and tracked the suspects to Mississauga, about a 45 minute drive from the scene, insauga.com said. Police recovered both the stolen vehicle and the stolen merchandise during the arrest, according to the outlet. Investigators did not release further details about how the arrest unfolded or where the vehicle had originally been stolen from.
